Hi Olivia — great context, thanks. Wanted to provide a concise packaging + billing recommendation so you and your legal/procurement team have something concrete to evaluate.

High-level recommendation (aligned to Acme needs):
1) Hosted (recommended initial path) — 12-month commit option
   - Why: Fastest onboarding, Redwood manages runtime and autoscaling; we can offer a committed discount for a 12-month baseline that covers predictable throughput.
   - Billing: Contract + PO (net30) works fine; we can also support monthly invoicing against the PO.
   - Marketplace: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace for hosted metered billing. For committed pricing via Marketplace we typically do a Contracted SaaS agreement + Marketplace listing — our team can walk you through pros/cons.

2) Dedicated (recommended if throughput predictability & isolation are top priorities)
   - Why: Dedicated GPU pools with reserved capacity and stronger isolation. Often chosen by platform teams that need guaranteed baseline throughput.
   - Commercial: Requires a reserved capacity commitment (monthly or annual). Pricing reflects the reserved baseline + overage pricing. PO + contract is standard; we can structure as monthly invoices against the committed contract.

3) Private / On-prem (only if required by compliance)
   - Why: For customers with strict network/isolation needs. This route typically involves higher implementation effort and an enterprise licensing/support fee.

Commit vs on-demand guidance:
- Commits (12-month baseline): 20–30% unit cost reduction vs pure on-demand; preferred if you need predictable unit economics and want to avoid spikes in monthly spend.
- On-demand / metered: flexible, no minimums, available via hosted or Marketplace, but unit cost is higher and capacity guarantees are weaker.

PO vs Card:
- PO (net30): straightforward for committed commercial terms. We will supply an invoice template and our billing contact to populate the PO.
- Card: OK for pilot phases under $10k/month; not recommended for full production.

Attachments I’m sending:
- Redwood_MSLA_v2_redline.pdf (initial MSLA for legal)
- pricing_estimate_acme_v2.xlsx (updated commercial options: hosted commit vs dedicated commit vs on-demand)

1) I’ll share the updated pricing spreadsheet + redlined MSLA (attached) for your legal team to review.
2) Dev — can you + Olivia schedule a 30-min procurement + tech sync this week to confirm SOW and PO fields (technical contacts, billing address, WBS line items)?
3) Once legal confirms MSLA redlines, we’ll send a DocuSign contract and a HubSpot link for the deal — you can issue a PO against the signed agreement.

If you’d like, we can also prepare an AWS Marketplace brief that explains metered vs contracted Marketplace options.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the pricing_estimate_acme_v2.xlsx.

Best,
